method.model: performance(m,b) = sigmoid(slope_b * (C_m - D_b) + offset_{b,group}), fitted by ridge-regularised non-linear least squares (same functional form as Epoch AI's ECI)
method.scale: C is on the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) scale because difficulty D_b and slope of every Epoch-tracked coding benchmark are fixed to the values published in Epoch AI's edi_scores.csv; other benchmarks are linked through models measured on both
method.benchmarks: coding benchmarks only; reasoning, knowledge, general chat and tool-use benchmarks are excluded; preference Elo (Arena WebDev) is validation only
method.artificial_analysis: Intelligence Index v5 is a weighted composite of pass rates and Elo-normalised components. Scores are not comparable across index versions and are not success probabilities, so the index is not divided by 100 and is not a likelihood term. The pre-v5 Coding Index (0-100) is still accepted as a validation series when an older API snapshot is the latest one. Current AA data enters the fit as per-benchmark fractions: LiveCodeBench, SciCode, Terminal-Bench Hard, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Terminal-Bench 4.0 join those existing series; FrontierCode 1.1 (AA) and FrontierCode 2.0 (AA) are separate unanchored benchmarks because they are not Epoch's FrontierCode item set. Terminal-Bench 4.0 is not written onto the Epoch-anchored Terminal Bench series. Progress Index v1 is an external general-capability check (o3-mini high = 220, GPT-5.5 xhigh = 320), not a coding observation. Within a canonical model the highest effort variant is kept, which is the existing one-value rule.
method.selection: one value per model and benchmark: third-party standard harness > third-party leaderboard with participant-built agents > unknown provenance > vendor self-report; within the best available tier, the highest value (highest reasoning effort)
method.offsets: leaderboard, unknown and self-reported values are shifted by the per-benchmark median logit gap against standard-harness values of the same models, shrunk toward the pooled gap (k = 5); leaderboard values on benchmarks without any standard-harness run are used as-is
method.uncertainty: bootstrap over each model's observations (Epoch-style), B = 200, seed = 7; CI = 2.5/97.5 percentiles
method.family_scores: C refitted per family with all benchmark parameters fixed; security benchmarks (ExploitBench, Cybench) only feed the security sub-score and are excluded from the overall coding score
method.low_information: models with only self-reported observations and a 95% CI wider than 1500 score points are moved to the estimated table and are not used as interpolation anchors
method.missing_models: models without coding observations are linearly interpolated by release date between the nearest measured models before and after them in the same series; no extrapolation
method.benchmark_rule: a benchmark needs >= 5 models and must be connected to the Epoch-anchored benchmarks through shared models

validation.definition: For each leaderboard, take every pair of models whose scores on that leaderboard differ by at least 10% of its score range and, when the leaderboard publishes standard errors, by more than 1.96 x the combined standard error and count the pairs whose order is reversed by the unified score. Target: below 5% per leaderboard.

SWE-rebench (common windows).note: pairwise on each pair's common task window (>= 60 days), as the leaderboard shows when that window is selected

established_pairs.definition: Point estimate of the coding score among models with a measured fit. Interpolated models are reported as unmeasured. A clear inversion means the weaker model's entire 95% interval sits above the stronger model's.

pairs.why: OpenAI flagship two generations above GPT-4o

progress_index.scale: o3-mini (high) = 220, GPT-5.5 (xhigh) = 320; general capability, not a coding probability

intelligence_index_v5.reason: v5 is a weighted mix of pass rates and Elo-normalised components. Scores are not comparable with v4.3 and are missing for models that were not rerun, including GPT-4o and GPT-5.5 in this snapshot.

coding_category_v5.definition: 0.60 * FrontierCode-AA 2.0 + 0.40 * Terminal-Bench 4.0, the v5 coding category (15% and 10% of the index). Not an independent check: those benchmarks are fit inputs.

naive_anchor_if_new_scores_replace_old_b.definition: Single-benchmark capability if Terminal-Bench 4.0 were scored on Epoch's Terminal Bench anchor (the 2.x leaderboard) or FrontierCode 2.0 on Epoch's FrontierCode anchor, for models the Progress Index places above GPT-4o. min of the two implied capabilities.

naive_refit.treatment: For models with a Terminal-Bench 4.0 score, delete every Terminal-Bench observation and write that 4.0 rate onto Terminal-Bench 2.0, which is anchored to Epoch's Terminal Bench difficulty. Do the same for FrontierCode 2.0 onto the anchored FrontierCode series. Also add Intelligence Index v5 divided by 100 as if it were a success probability. One refit, no bootstrap.
